ops.insert: OpenAI’s $6.5 Billion Bet on Jony Ive Reveals the Skill Technology Can’t Replace

Silicon Valley’s new obsession with “taste” reveals something every leader needs to understand about where competitive advantage is heading. 

The term has become Silicon Valley’s newest cliché, with technologist Paul Graham posting that “in the

age, taste will become even more important,” Framer founder Koen Bok calling “great taste” the key differentiator for new products, and former ByteDance engineer Cong Wang writing that “personal taste is the moat.” 
The piece arrived months after

completed a $5 billion acquisition of design icon Jony Ive’s company io, betting that Ive’s judgment about what to build is worth more than anything its own engineers could generate alone. 
Over at

, a parallel story has been unfolding: the company’s design studio has shed nearly every Ive-era designer. Incoming CEO John Ternus may find himself focusing on rebuilding the brand’s design credibility. The debate Chayka started is about something much bigger than aesthetics.
